passages.note: Bill overview lists Carter as a co-sponsor of HB2492, chaptered into law 2022-03-30.
House Third Reading roll call shows Carter voting Y on final passage of HB2492, which passed 31-26-3-0-0.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted bill text requires satisfactory evidence of citizenship before a registration application is accepted, rejecting applications lacking it.

rows.reasoning: Carter co-sponsored and voted Yea on HB2492 (2022), a single-subject Arizona law that requires 'satisfactory evidence of citizenship' before an application for registration is accepted, rejecting applications that lack it. This matches rung 5, 'Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote,' and the 31-26-3-0-0 final vote was not near-unanimous.
